_why: A rename that is only remembered is a rename that drifts. Every one of these
was found in 2026-09 by tripping over it: a public page linking a host that
only redirects, a studio page naming a product by its repo name, a register
row pointing at a directory that had moved. None of them broke anything, and
that is the problem — a 308 answers 200, so a stale address looks healthy.
Recording a retirement here is what lets org-drift-audit.sh find documents
still using the old form. A new retirement is a ROW, not a code change.
`from` must be specific enough not to fire on prose. A host or a product
name is safe; a bare word like 'sink' is not, and does not belong here.

_fields.from: the retired form — what a document should no longer say
_fields.since: ISO date the replacement became true
_fields.why: one line, so the entry can be judged rather than obeyed
_fields.verified: how the retirement was confirmed, not who asserted it
